description: Dataflow analysis decomposed. The framework: lattice + transfer function + meet operator + iteration to fixed point. Reaching definitions, live variables, available expressions, constant propagation, points-to analysis. Forward vs backward. May vs must. The mathematical foundation of compiler analysis.

sub_mechanisms.name: lattice
sub_mechanisms.definition: Partially-ordered set with meets (greatest lower bound). Dataflow values live in a lattice; analysis computes the appropriate element per program point.
sub_mechanisms.why: Mathematical framework. Bottom = no information; top = no constraints; meet combines information from different paths. Lattice properties ensure convergence.

sub_mechanisms.name: transfer_function
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-statement function: how does this statement transform dataflow information? e.g., 'x = 5' kills any prior definition of x + generates the new one.
sub_mechanisms.why: Per-statement effects. Composing transfer functions along a path gives the path's overall effect. Statement-by-statement is how analysis advances.

sub_mechanisms.name: meet_operator
sub_mechanisms.definition: Combines dataflow information from different control-flow paths. For 'live variables' (may analysis): union. For 'available expressions' (must analysis): intersection.
sub_mechanisms.why: Control-flow joins require combining incoming information. Choice of meet (union vs intersection) distinguishes may from must analyses. Determines what 'reaches' a program point.

sub_mechanisms.name: may_analysis
sub_mechanisms.definition: Information from ANY path. Live variables: variable might be used on some future path. Reaching definitions: definition might reach this point.
sub_mechanisms.why: Conservative for optimisations that need 'is it safe?': if no path uses x, we can kill it. Union as meet operator. Standard for liveness, pointer analysis.

sub_mechanisms.name: must_analysis
sub_mechanisms.definition: Information from ALL paths. Available expressions: expression must be computed on every path. Constants: value must be the same on all paths.
sub_mechanisms.why: Conservative for optimisations that need 'is it always true?': if x must be constant, replace it. Intersection as meet operator. Standard for available expressions, constant propagation.

sub_mechanisms.name: forward_analysis
sub_mechanisms.definition: Information flows from program start toward end. Information at point P depends on predecessors.
sub_mechanisms.why: Natural for: 'what definitions reach here?' (reaching definitions), 'what expressions are available?'. Iterate by walking forward through CFG.

sub_mechanisms.name: backward_analysis
sub_mechanisms.definition: Information flows from program end toward start. Information at point P depends on successors.
sub_mechanisms.why: Natural for: 'what will be used in the future?' (live variables), 'what does this point dominate?'. Iterate by walking backward through CFG.

sub_mechanisms.name: iterative_fixed_point
sub_mechanisms.definition: Initialise dataflow values; iterate transfer functions + meet operator until values stop changing. Result is a fixed point.
sub_mechanisms.why: Lattice's finite descending chain condition guarantees termination. The fixed point IS the analysis result. Standard implementation: worklist algorithm prioritising blocks whose inputs changed.

sub_mechanisms.name: monotone_framework
sub_mechanisms.definition: If lattice is finite + transfer functions are monotone (more input information → more output information), iterative analysis converges.
sub_mechanisms.why: Kildall's theorem (1973). Monotonicity + finite lattice = guaranteed termination at unique fixed point. Underlies all classical dataflow analyses.

sub_mechanisms.name: reaching_definitions
sub_mechanisms.definition: At each program point, which definitions could provide the current value of each variable? Forward, may analysis.
sub_mechanisms.why: Powers def-use chains, constant propagation, dead code elimination. Standard textbook analysis. Generalises to SSA's φ functions: each variable has one definition reaching each point.

sub_mechanisms.name: live_variable_analysis
sub_mechanisms.definition: At each program point, which variables will be used before being redefined? Backward, may analysis.
sub_mechanisms.why: Required for register allocation (interference graph), dead store elimination. Foundational backward dataflow. live_out[B] = ∪ live_in[succ]; live_in[B] = use[B] ∪ (live_out[B] - def[B]).

sub_mechanisms.name: available_expressions
sub_mechanisms.definition: At each program point, which expressions have been computed and not invalidated? Forward, must analysis.
sub_mechanisms.why: Powers common subexpression elimination. If expression e is available at P, the computation can be replaced with the saved value. Intersection meet: must be available on all paths.

derivation_rules.name: Kildall_theorem_iterative_convergence
if: lattice is finite and transfer functions are monotone
then: iterative analysis converges to the maximum fixed point
derivation_rules.why: Foundational result. Monotonicity ensures information doesn't oscillate; finiteness ensures finite chain of improvements. The result is the most precise solution consistent with the analysis framework.

derivation_rules.name: meet_operator_distinguishes_may_must
derivation_rules.why: Union accumulates: any source contributes. Intersection requires consensus: all sources must agree. The meet operator's identity IS the distinction between may and must analyses. Determines what 'arrives' at a control-flow join.

derivation_rules.name: forward_analysis_natural_for_origin_tracking
if: analysis tracks where information came from
derivation_rules.why: Reaching definitions, available expressions both track 'what produced this value/expression'. Information flows from production toward use. Forward iteration matches the dataflow direction.

derivation_rules.name: backward_analysis_natural_for_future_use
if: analysis tracks what will use information
derivation_rules.why: Live variables, very busy expressions track 'what future code needs'. Information flows from use back toward production. Backward iteration matches the demand direction.

derivation_rules.name: live_variable_analysis_powers_register_allocation
if: liveness is known at each program point
then: interference graph for register allocation can be built
derivation_rules.why: Two variables interfere iff both live at some point. Liveness gives the live ranges; intersections give interferences. Register allocation directly depends on liveness analysis quality.
